Agreement No. CE 35/2023 (HY)
Development of the Loop: Eastern Connection Road -
Investigation, Design and Construction EIA Report
LAND CONTAMINATION
Introduction
This section presents potential land contamination implications associated with the
Project. Land contamination implications were assessed in accordance with Clause
3.5.7 and Appendix F of the EIA Study Brief (No. ESB-375/2025).
Environmental Legislation, Standards and Guidelines
The relevant environmental legislation guidelines and standards on land contamination
aspect include the following:-
• Section 3 (Potential Contaminated Land Issues) of Annex 19 "Guidelines for
Assessment of Impact on Sites of Cultural Heritage and Other Impacts" of the
Technical Memorandum on Environmental Impact Assessment Process (EIAO-
TM).
• Guidance Note for Contaminated Land Assessment and Remediation (Guidance
Note)
This Guidance Note sets out the requirements for the proper assessment and
management of potentially contaminated sites such as oil installations (e.g. oil
depots, petrol filling stations), gas works, power plants, shipyards / boatyards,
chemical manufacturing / processing plants, steel mills / metal workshops, car
repairing / dismantling workshops and scrap yards. In addition, this Guidance
Note provides guidelines on how site assessments should be conducted and
evaluated and suggests practical remedial measures that can be adopted for the
remediation of contaminated sites.
• Practice Guide for Investigation and Remediation of Contaminated Land (Practice
Guide)
This guide outlines typical investigation methods and remediation strategies for
the range of potential contaminants typically encountered in Hong Kong.
• Guidance Manual for Use of Risk-based Remediation Goals for Contaminated
Land Management (Guidance Manual)
This Guidance Manual introduces the risk-based approach in land contamination
assessment and provides details for the comparison of soil and groundwater data
under Risk-Based Remediation Goals (RBRGs) for 54 chemicals of concern
(COCs) commonly found in Hong Kong. The RBRGs were derived to suit Hong
Kong conditions by following the international practice of adopting a risk-based
methodology for contaminated land assessment and remediation; and were
designed to protect the health of people who could potentially be exposed to land
impacted by chemicals under four broad post restoration land use categories. The
RBRGs also serve as the remediation targets where remediation is necessary.

Agreement No. CE 35/2023 (HY)
Development of the Loop: Eastern Connection Road -
Investigation, Design and Construction EIA Report
Assessment Methodology
Land contamination assessment was undertaken in accordance with the EIAO-TM,
Guidance Note, Practice Guide and Guidance Manual, and the requirements stated in
Clause 3.5.7 and Appendix F of the EIA Study Brief.
The following tasks were undertaken to identify any potentially contaminated areas for
the purpose of land contamination assessment:
• Site walkover to identify the potentially contaminated sites; and
• Desktop review of site history.
For the desktop review, the following information was reviewed:
• Topographic maps and relevant aerial photographs (Lands Department);
• Hong Kong Geological Survey Maps and previous ground investigation records;
• Relevant EIA reports and Project Profiles
• Records of dangerous goods and chemical spillage/leakage incidents (Fire
Services Department, FSD);
• Chemical waste producer register and chemical spillage/leakage incidents
(Environmental Protection Department, EPD); and
• Geochemical Atlas of Hong Kong.
Description of Environment
The Project is located at the Loop, Ma Tso Lung and the rural areas connecting them
with the land use comprising fishponds, rural roads (connecting Lok Ma Chau and Ma
Tso Lung) and Ma Tso Lung Shun Yee San Tsuen. The Project location is shown in
60722948/A10/FIGURE 2.1.
Identification of Potential Land Contamination Concern
Site Walkover
Site walkover was conducted in May 2024, August 2024 and March 2025. Photographs
taken during the site walkover are provided in Appendix 7.1. A site walkover checklist
is provided in Appendix 7.2. Based on the findings of the Site walkover, no potential
land contamination activity or hotspots were identified within Project boundary or in off-
site areas immediately adjacent to the Project Site except for at site MTL-001 along Ma
Tso Lung Road.
Site MTL-001 was an open storage for construction company. The site was
inaccessible during site visit. The site walkover was conducted through peripheral
inspection and drone reconnaissance. The site was an equipment/machinery open
storage with potential maintenance and small diesel storage. Equipment and machines
(drill rig, pumping, casing/drill rod) for ground investigation were observed on site.
Storage of diesel and maintenance of drill rig is anticipated on site. The location of site
MTL-001 is provided in 60722948/A10/FIGURE 7.4.

Agreement No. CE 35/2023 (HY)

Investigation, Design and Construction EIA Report
According to the 1:20,000 Hong Kong Geological Survey (HKGS) Solid and Superficial
Geology Map Sheet 2 (2022) and Solid Geology Map Sheet 2 (2022), superficial
geology is represented by pond deposits, estuarine deposits, marine deposits, alluvium
and colluvium. The underlying solid geology includes the Mai Po Member (mainly
metasiltstone, metasandstone and graphite-bearing) (Cslm) of the Lok Ma Chau
Formation and Tai Shek Mo Member (mainly metasandstone with metaconglomerate
and phyllite) (Cslt) of Lok Ma Chau Formation. Medium-grained granite (gm) is mapped
at the northwest portion of the Site. The HKGS Solid and Superficial Geology Map is
provided in 60722948/A10/FIGURE 7.5.
Superficial Geology - Superficial deposits including fill, pond, marine and estuarine
deposits, alluvium, and colluvium are further described as follows.
• Fill is inferred to occur at the developed areas, in particular the former Central
Government-Aided Emergency Hospital area. The fill is anticipated to be
generally absent in undeveloped areas and natural hillsides within the Project.
• Pond deposits (PD) are anticipated at the location of current and previous ponds
mainly located in the vicinity of the central portion of the Site based on information
from Map Sheet 2, topographical maps and aerial photographs. PD are
anticipated to be underlain by estuarine deposits, marine deposit, alluvium and
in-situ materials.
• Intertidal deposits Qhi (ED) are anticipated in places in the vicinity of pond areas
to the south of Shenzhen River. ED are anticipated to be overlain by fill or PD
and underlain by alluvium and/or in-situ materials.
• Alluvial deposits (including Alluvium Qfa) are anticipated within the majority
footprint of the Site and are anticipated to be partially overlain by fill, PD, ED
and/or MD.
• Colluvium (COLL) or debris flow deposit Qd/Qcd may be encountered at the
footslopes of hillsides at Ping Hang and Ma Tso Lung. COLL is typically underlain
by in-situ materials.
Solid Geology - The Site area is underlain by complex solid geology with rock types
including:
• Lok Ma Chau Formation (Mai Po Member) (Cslm) to the northwestern side of the
Ma Tso Lung Fault and southeast of Yuen Tau Shan Fault, i.e., to the northwest
of Pang Hang; and also in general area near Lo Wu Range located at the southern
portion of the Site. The LMC formation (Mai Po Member) typically consists of
meta-sedimentary rocks including metasiltstone, metasandstone and graphite-
bearing rocks.
• Lok Ma Chau Formation (Tai Shek Mo Member) (Cslt) generally located to the
southeastern side of the Ma Tso Lung Fault, at Ma Tso Lung area where hilly
terrain exists. The LMC formation (Tai Shek Mo Member) typically consists of
meta-sedimentary rocks including meta-sandstone with metaconglomerate and
phyllite.

Review of Previous EIA Study
The following EIA reports and Project Profiles (for permission to apply directly for an
Environmental Permit) were reviewed.
• Development of Lok Ma Chau Loop EIA Report (EIA Register No. AEIAR-
176/2013)
• Construction of a Secondary Boundary Fence and new sections of Primary
Boundary Fence and Boundary Patrol Road EIA Report (EIA Register No. AEIAR-
136/2009)
• Project Profile for Installation of the Proposed 132kV Cable Circuits Connecting
with Ho To West Substation and Existing 132kV Fanling to Mai Po Cable Circuits
(Application No. DIR-284/2021)
• Project Profile for New Boundary Bridge between Lok Ma Chau and Huanggang
(Application No. DIR-081/2003)
No potentially contaminated sites were identified in the Construction of a Secondary
Boundary Fence and new sections of Primary Boundary Fence and Boundary Patrol
Road EIA Report (EIA Register No. AEIAR-136/2009) and the Project Profiles for
Installation of the Proposed 132kV Cable Circuits Connecting with Ho To West
Substation and Existing 132kV Fanling to Mai Po Cable Circuits (Application No. DIR-
284/2021) and New Boundary Bridge between Lok Ma Chau and Huanggang
(Application No. DIR-081/2003).
With reference to the EIA report for Development of Lok Ma Chau Loop (EIA Register
No. AEIAR-176/2013), potential land contamination was anticipated as a result of
disposal of contaminated mud within the Loop (Potential Contaminated Site A) in year
1995 -2000. The depth of disposed mud was anticipated to be approximately 5m
(including 1m to 1.5m thickness of a top layer of uncontaminated mud for capping). Site
investigation works within the Loop included investigation to a maximum depth of 5m
based on the depth of disposed mud. The study area of EIA report for Development of
the Loop and the Potential Contaminated Site A is shown in 60722948/A10/FIGURE
7.2. Previous site investigation locations under the EIA for the Development of the Loop
are provided in 60722948/A10/FIGURE 7.2. Relevant reports from the EIA reports
(Appendix 8-2) are extracted and provided in Appendix 7.4.
The concentration of the metal “Arsenic (As)” in 6 soil samples collected from 5
boreholes marginally exceeded the Risk-Based Remediation Goals (RBRGs) for Rural
Residential and Urban Residential land uses. The 5 boreholes, namely A-S01, A-S01,
A-S03, A-S03a and A-S03c1, are not situated within the Project Boundary. However
the contaminated areas as identified in the Remediation Action Plan are shown in
60722948/A10/FIGURE 7.2. Following implementation of the Remediation Action Plan
during the construction phase; all contaminated soils will be remediated. No
groundwater contamination was detected.

Agreement No. CE 35/2023 (HY)
Development of the Loop: Eastern Connection Road -
Investigation, Design and Construction EIA Report
Remediation for arsenic contamination within the Loop was completed by Contract No.
YL/2017/03 - Development of the Loop – land decontamination and advance
engineering works. Arsenic contaminated soils were treated by cement
solidification/stabilisation and backfilled on site.
The previous soil and groundwater test results in the Loop compared against the lower
of Industrial or Public Park RBRGs are summarised in Appendix 7.5. With reference
to Section 2, this Project will consist of a depressed/underpass/at grade and viaduct
road, footpath, plant room/control room, noise barrier and other ancillary works. The
corresponding RBRGs for this project are the “Lower of Industrial or Public Park” as per
the Guidance Manual. Although the EIA report reports RBRG exceedance for Arsenic
for the Urban Residential and Rural Residential land use scenarios, no exceedance of
the lower of Industrial or Public Park RBRGs or soil saturation limits / solubility limits
were identified from comparison of previous soil and groundwater testing results. No
land contamination associated with mud disposal within the Loop is identified.
Information from Government Departments
The EPD and FSD were contacted to obtain;
• records of any spillage / leakage of chemicals;
• records of Dangerous Goods (DG);
• records of Chemical Waste Producer(s) (CWPs); and
• records of reported incidents within the Project area.
EPD and FSD's replies on the request are presented in Appendices 7.6 and 7.7,
respectively. The information is summarised below.
Environmental Protection Department
Based on EPD replies dated 13 March 2024, 3 September 2024 and 20 August 2025
regarding requests for chemical spillage/ leakage information, EPD has no record of
any chemical spillage / leakage within the Project area. EPD Environmental
Compliance Division, Territorial Control Office, Chemical Waste and WEEE (Licensing
and Control Support) Section was visited on 8 February 2024 and 12 August 2025 to
review CWP records. No CWPs were identified within the Project area.
Fire Services Department
Records of any Dangerous Goods Store(s) and any reported accidents or
spillage/leakage within the Project area were requested from FSD. FSD had three letter
replies on 12 April 2024, 24 September 2024, and 29 August 2025. No Dangerous
Goods store is recorded within the Project area. A total of thirteen (13) individual
incidents were reported by FSD with twelve of them being rubbish fire, vegetation fire
or No. 1 fire alarm. The approximate location of the incident is provided in
60722948/A10/FIGURE 7.3.
One of 13 incidents (Event No. FSD10) was chemical spillage in Central Government
Aided Emergency Hospital. There was leakage of suspected peroxyacetic acid from 2
nos. of 5-litre plastic containers. It is reported that FSD cleaned up the spilled with

Geochemical Atlas of Hong Kong
With reference to the Preliminary Feasibility Study on Developing the New Territories
North, the Geochemical Atlas of Hong Kong published by the Geotechnical Engineering
Office of Civil Engineering and Development Department in 1999 and the Hong Kong
Environmental Database (HKED) by EPD, natural occurrences of elevated level of

arsenic assessment and remediation plan should be prepared and submitted to EPD
for endorsement.
Prediction and Evaluation of Environmental Impacts
Based on the findings from desktop review (e.g. review of historical aerial photographs
and relevant information from EPD and FSD, examination of previous EIA reports and
site investigation records) and a site walkover; no land use with potential to give rise to
land contamination is identified within Project boundary or at off-site areas immediately
adjacent to the Project Site except for Site MTL-001.
Site MTL-001 was a construction company storage yard which is identified as a
potentially contaminated site. Possible contaminating activities may have resulted from
release of oils and fuels and lubricants from vehicles/plant during storage, maintenance
or refuelling as well as storage and use of chemicals and solvents required for
maintenance activities and possible waste arisings. A site appraisal report (SAP) for
site MTL-001 is provided in Appendix 7.8. The location of site MTL-001 is provided in
60722948/A10/FIGURE 7.4.
Previous Development of the Loop EIA report identified arsenic contaminated soils
within the Loop assuming post redevelopment Rural Residential and Urban Residential
land uses scenarios. Remediation works for arsenic contamination with the Loop was
completed by Contract No. YL/2017/03 - Development of the Loop – land
decontamination and advance engineering works. All identified arsenic contaminated
soils were treated by cement solidification/stabilisation and backfilled on site.
Site investigation works within the Loop cover a depth of 5m for the previous
contaminated mud disposal. A further review of soil and groundwater test results
identified no exceedance of the lower of Industrial or Public Park RBRGs and no
exceedance of soil saturation limit/solubility limits are identified. No land contamination
is identified as a result of previous contaminated mud disposal.
As no land contamination impact arising from the Project is anticipated; no mitigation
measures are necessary and no further site investigation for land contamination is
required except for Site MTL-001.

The area within the Project boundary will remain in operation and potential exists for a
change in land use or operations prior to development. It is recommended to re-
appraise the whole area within the Project boundary once the Project Site is resumed
and fully accessible. If there are land use changes which pose a potential for land
contamination, this information should be reported in Contamination Assessment Plan
(CAP) for potentially contaminated sites.
Prior to construction at potentially contaminated sites, the Project Proponent should
appoint a consultant to re-appraise the site and update the findings (e.g. locations of
hotspots) and sampling and testing requirements presented in the SAP, once the
Project Site is resumed and fully accessible. A CAP shall be prepared based on the
findings in the SAP alongside incorporating the additional assessment and evaluation
findings of the site re-appraisal and the updated sampling and testing strategy should
be prepared and submitted to EPD for approval prior to conducting any SI works.
SI works should be implemented according to the CAP. A Contamination Assessment
Report (CAR) detailing the findings and, if contaminated soil and/or groundwater is
identified, a Remediation Action Plan (RAP) should be prepared and submitted to EPD
for approval. Any contaminated soil and groundwater should be treated according to
EPD’s approved RAP and a Remediation Report (RR) should be submitted to EPD for
agreement after completion of the remediation works. No construction or development
works should be carried out on potentially contaminated site prior to EPD approval of
the CAP, and CAR and/or RR, if necessary.
With reference to the Preliminary Feasibility Study on Developing the New Territories
North, the Geochemical Atlas of Hong Kong published by the Geotechnical Engineering
Office of Civil Engineering and Development Department in 1999 and the Hong Kong
Environmental Database (HKED) by EPD, natural occurrences of elevated level of
arsenic exist over broad areas of the northern New Territories. A separate arsenic
assessment and remediation plan should be prepared and submitted to EPD for
endorsement.
Evaluation of Residual Impacts
Referring to Section 8 of the SAP (Appendix 7.8), land contamination issues are
surmountable. If the recommended further works in Section 7.7 are followed and
contaminated soil and groundwater (if any) is properly treated using appropriate
remediation methods and according to EPD’s approved RAP. However, any localised
soil/groundwater contamination within these sites, if left untreated, could potentially
pose health risks to existing or future occupants.
By implementing the recommended further works under this Project, any contaminated
soil and groundwater would be identified and treated. The recommended further works
would not only minimise the health risk to future occupants arising from exposure to
contaminated soil and/or groundwater, it would also provide the opportunity to treat the
contaminated soil / groundwater using proven remediation techniques for reuse as
useful materials (such as backfilling materials).
Environmental Monitoring and Audit
Remediation works, if necessary, would be carried out based on the recommended
further works outlined in Section 7.7. Mitigation measures as recommended in the

Conclusion
This land contamination assessment assessed the potential for contaminative land use
within the Project boundary. Based on the findings of desktop review (e.g. a review of
historical aerial photographs and relevant information from EPD and FSD) and a site
walkover; no potential land contaminating land use was identified except for
Site MTL-001. Site MTL-001 was inaccessible during site visit. The site walkover was
conducted through peripheral inspection and drone reconnaissance. The site was a
construction company storage yard which is identified as a potentially contaminated
site. Possible contaminating activities may have resulted from release of oils and fuels
and lubricants from vehicles/plant during storage, maintenance or refuelling as well as
storage and use of chemicals and solvents required for maintenance activities and
possible waste arisings.
It is recommended to re-appraise the whole area within the Project boundary once the
Project Site is resumed and fully accessible prior to development. Further works,
including site re-appraisal, SI works as well as submission of a CAP and CAR for EPD’s
endorsement are recommended to be carried out after the Project site is handed over
to the PP for development. If contaminated soil and/or groundwater is identified;
remediation should be carried out according to the EPD approved RAP and a RR
should be submitted to EPD for agreement after completion of the remediation works.
No construction or development works should be carried out on potentially
contaminated sites prior to EPD approval of the CAP, and CAR and/or RR, if necessary.
With reference to previous studies, natural occurrences of elevated level of arsenic
exist over broad areas of the northern New Territories. A separate arsenic assessment
and remediation plan should be prepared and submitted to EPD for endorsement.
With the implementation of the recommended further works, any soil/groundwater
contamination would be identified and properly treated prior to the construction works.
No insurmountable land contamination impacts to the Project are therefore anticipated.
